title: [Pallas] interpret=True silently drops intermediate block writes (outputs NaN) when tiling last dimension with >=3 blocks
author: ShinapriLN

comments.author: vfdev-5
comments.body:
@ShinapriLN I think the problem you see is related to incorrect BlockSpecs for input and output. You implement in the element mode, but they should be in block mode: https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/pallas/grid_blockspec.html#the-element-indexing-mode

```diff
- index_map=lambda i, j: (i, j * block_size),
+ index_map=lambda i, j: (i, j),
```


For example, the copy kernel with less trivial input shows exactly what we expect:
```python
import os
os.environ["JAX_PLATFORMS"] = "cpu"

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import jax.experimental.pallas as pl


def copy_kernel(x_ref, out_ref):
    """Trivial kernel — copies input to output. No computation."""
    out_ref[...] = x_ref[...]

def run_copy_test(shape, block_size, label):
    """Run the trivial copy kernel and check for NaN."""
    N, C = shape
    n_blocks = C // block_size

    dtype = jnp.float32
    x = jnp.arange(N * C, dtype=dtype).reshape(shape)

    out = pl.pallas_call(
        copy_kernel,
        out_shape=jax.ShapeDtypeStruct(shape, dtype),
        grid=(N, n_blocks),
        in_specs=[pl.BlockSpec(
            index_map=lambda i, j: (i, j),
            block_shape=(1, block_size),
        )],
        out_specs=pl.BlockSpec(
            index_map=lambda i, j: (i, j),
            block_shape=(1, block_size),
        ),
        interpret=True,
    )(x)

    has_nan = bool(jnp.isnan(out).any())
    nan_count = int(jnp.isnan(out).sum()) if has_nan else 0
    status = f"✗ NaN ({nan_count}/{out.size} elements)" if has_nan else "✓ OK"
    print(f"  {label:<50s} blocks={n_blocks:<3d} {status}")
    print(f"{out[0, 125:125 + 10]=}")
    return out


def main():
    block_size = 128
    for n_blocks in [1, 2, 3, 4, 8]:
        C = block_size * n_blocks
        out = run_copy_test((1, C), block_size, f"shape=(1, {C})")
        assert (out == jnp.arange(C, dtype=jnp.float32).reshape((1, -1))).all()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```


I haven't checked other kernels, but suppose that there is a similar problem
